entries.name: Temporary Files
entries.explanation: Files that apps and installers leave in your temp folder and forget to remove. Only items nobody has touched for a day are included, and anything still open is skipped.

entries.name: Crash Dumps
entries.explanation: Memory snapshots Windows saves when an app crashes, for the developer to debug. Safe to clean unless you were about to send one to support.

entries.name: Error Reports
entries.explanation: Problem reports Windows Error Reporting has queued or already sent to Microsoft. Safe to clean; Windows writes new ones if something crashes again.

entries.name: Windows Web Cache
entries.explanation: Web pages and images cached by Windows components and older apps that use the system web engine. Safe to clean; files are downloaded again when needed.

entries.name: DirectX Shader Cache
entries.explanation: Compiled graphics shaders Windows keeps so games and apps start faster. Safe to clean. The first launch of a game afterwards may stutter briefly while shaders compile again.

entries.name: NVIDIA Shader Cache
entries.explanation: Compiled shaders the NVIDIA driver caches for games and apps. Safe to clean. Games rebuild them on their next launch, which may cause brief stutters.

entries.name: AMD Shader Cache
entries.explanation: Compiled shaders the AMD driver caches for games and apps. Safe to clean. Games rebuild them on their next launch, which may cause brief stutters.

entries.name: Intel Shader Cache
entries.explanation: Compiled shaders the Intel graphics driver caches for games and apps. Safe to clean; they are rebuilt as you play.

entries.name: Google Chrome Cache
entries.explanation: Pages, images and scripts Chrome saved so sites load faster, for every Chrome profile. Your bookmarks, passwords, history and sign-ins are not touched. Sites may load a little slower at first.

entries.name: Microsoft Edge Cache
entries.explanation: Pages, images and scripts Edge saved so sites load faster, for every Edge profile. Your favorites, passwords, history and sign-ins are not touched. Sites may load a little slower at first.

entries.name: Brave Cache
entries.explanation: Pages, images and scripts Brave saved so sites load faster, for every Brave profile. Your bookmarks, passwords, history and wallet are not touched.

entries.name: Vivaldi Cache
entries.explanation: Pages, images and scripts Vivaldi saved so sites load faster. Your bookmarks, passwords, notes and history are not touched.

entries.name: Opera Cache
entries.explanation: Pages, images and scripts Opera saved so sites load faster. Your bookmarks, passwords and history are not touched.

entries.name: Firefox Cache
entries.explanation: Pages, images and scripts Firefox saved so sites load faster, for every Firefox profile. Your bookmarks, passwords, history and add-ons live elsewhere and are not touched.

entries.name: Steam Web Cache
entries.explanation: Store pages, images and community content cached by the Steam client. Your games and saves are not touched. Steam downloads what it needs again.

entries.name: Adobe Media Cache Files
entries.explanation: Premiere Pro and After Effects store rendered previews and conformed audio here. Safe to clean. The apps rebuild it on next launch, which can take a few minutes for large projects.

closeFirst.app: Adobe Premiere Pro or After Effects

entries.name: iPhone and iPad Software Updates
entries.explanation: Copies of iOS and iPadOS that iTunes downloaded to update or restore a device, several gigabytes each. Safe to clean. iTunes downloads the current version again when a device needs it.

entries.name: Telegram Media Cache
entries.explanation: Photos, videos and voice messages Telegram Desktop kept after you viewed them. Your chats, and files you saved, are not touched. Safe to clean. Telegram downloads media again from its cloud when you open it.

entries.name: npm Package Cache
entries.explanation: Cached packages downloaded by npm, plus npx downloads and npm logs. Safe to delete and re-downloaded when you run npm install.

entries.name: pnpm Package Store
entries.explanation: The central package store pnpm shares across projects. Installed projects keep working; packages are downloaded again on the next pnpm install.

entries.name: Yarn Package Cache
entries.explanation: Cached packages downloaded by Yarn. Safe to delete and re-downloaded when you run yarn install.

entries.name: Bun Package Cache
entries.explanation: Cached packages downloaded by Bun. Safe to delete and re-downloaded the next time you run bun install.

entries.name: Deno Module Cache
entries.explanation: Modules and npm packages Deno downloaded and compiled. Saved local storage for Deno apps is left alone. Safe to delete; re-downloaded on your next run.

entries.name: Corepack Cache
entries.explanation: Package manager versions Corepack downloaded. Safe to delete; Corepack fetches them again on next use.

entries.name: Electron Download Cache
entries.explanation: Electron runtimes and build tools downloaded by electron and electron-builder. Safe to delete; downloaded again on your next install or build.

entries.name: NuGet HTTP Cache
entries.explanation: Package listings and downloads NuGet caches between restores. Safe to delete; the next restore fetches what it needs.

entries.name: NuGet Package Cache
entries.explanation: Downloaded .NET packages that NuGet restores your projects from. Nothing is lost, but your next restore downloads them all again, which can take a while and needs an internet connection.

entries.name: Gradle Dependency Cache
entries.explanation: Libraries, build caches and Gradle versions downloaded for Java, Kotlin and Android projects. Nothing is lost, but your next build downloads everything again, which can take a long time.

entries.name: Maven Package Cache
entries.explanation: Java libraries downloaded by Maven, plus anything you built and installed locally with mvn install. Downloaded libraries come back on your next build; locally installed ones need rebuilding.

entries.name: Ivy Dependency Cache
entries.explanation: Java and Scala libraries downloaded by sbt and Ivy. Nothing is lost, but your next build downloads all of them again.

entries.name: Android Build Cache
entries.explanation: Build caches Android Studio and Gradle keep in .android. Your emulators, the key your phones trust for debugging, and your debug signing key are left alone. Safe to delete; the next build recreates them.

entries.name: Rust Package Cache
entries.explanation: Crates and git dependencies Cargo downloaded. Your installed tools in .cargo\bin are left alone. Safe to delete; re-downloaded when you next build.

entries.name: Go Build and Module Cache
entries.explanation: Compiled Go packages and downloaded module archives. Safe to delete; rebuilt and re-downloaded when you build your Go projects again.

entries.name: pip Package Cache
entries.explanation: Python packages pip downloaded and built. Your installed packages and environments are not touched. Safe to delete; re-downloaded the next time you install.

entries.name: uv Package Cache
entries.explanation: Cached Python packages downloaded by uv. Python versions uv installed and your environments are left alone. Safe to delete; re-downloaded when you next install.

entries.name: Poetry Package Cache
entries.explanation: Package downloads and build artifacts Poetry caches. The virtual environments Poetry manages are left alone. Safe to delete.

entries.name: Conda Package Cache
entries.explanation: Packages conda downloaded and unpacked to build your environments. Environments may link to these files, so run conda clean --all yourself if you are unsure.

entries.name: pre-commit Environments
entries.explanation: Tool environments pre-commit sets up to run your git hooks. Safe to delete; they are set up again on your next commit, which makes that commit slower.

entries.name: Composer Cache
entries.explanation: Cached PHP packages downloaded by Composer. Safe to delete and re-downloaded when you run composer install.

entries.name: vcpkg Binary Cache
entries.explanation: Prebuilt C and C++ libraries vcpkg caches so it does not rebuild them. Safe to delete; the next install builds them again, which can be slow.

entries.name: Scoop Download Cache
entries.explanation: Installers Scoop downloaded. The apps you installed are not touched. Safe to delete; Scoop downloads them again if you reinstall.

entries.name: Terraform Plugin Cache
entries.explanation: Cached Terraform provider plugins. Safe to delete and re-downloaded when you run terraform init.

entries.name: Playwright Browsers
entries.explanation: Browsers Playwright downloaded for automated website testing. Your tests fail until you run npx playwright install, which downloads them again.

entries.name: Puppeteer Browsers
entries.explanation: Browsers Puppeteer downloaded for automated testing. Your scripts fail until the browser is installed again, which happens on your next npm install.

entries.name: Cypress Test Binaries
entries.explanation: The Cypress app downloaded for end-to-end testing. Cypress needs to download it again before your next test run.

entries.name: Visual Studio Code Cache
entries.explanation: Web content, compiled code and extension downloads VS Code caches. Your settings, extensions and workspaces are not touched. Safe to delete; rebuilt on next launch.

entries.name: Cursor Cache
entries.explanation: Web content, compiled code and extension downloads Cursor caches. Your settings, extensions, workspaces and chat history are not touched. Safe to delete; rebuilt on next launch.

entries.name: JetBrains IDE Caches
entries.explanation: Indexes and caches IntelliJ IDEA, Rider, PyCharm, WebStorm and other JetBrains IDEs build for your projects. Settings, plugins and Local History are left alone. The next time you open a project, the IDE re-indexes it, which can take a while.

entries.name: Visual Studio Component Cache
entries.explanation: The component catalog Visual Studio builds at startup. Safe to delete, and a common fix when Visual Studio misbehaves; it is rebuilt on next launch.

chromiumApps.explanation: Web content {app} saved so it loads faster. Your messages, files, settings and sign-in are stored elsewhere and are not touched. Safe to clean; {app} downloads what it needs again.

windowsCleanup.name: Windows Update Cleanup
windowsCleanup.explanation: Older copies of Windows components that newer updates replaced. Afterwards you can't uninstall the updates you have now. Checking and cleaning this one can take several minutes.

windowsCleanup.name: Delivery Optimization Files
windowsCleanup.explanation: Pieces of updates Windows downloaded and shares with other PCs. Safe to clean. Windows downloads what it needs again.

windowsCleanup.name: Previous Version of Windows
windowsCleanup.explanation: Your previous version of Windows, kept in Windows.old after an upgrade. Afterwards you can't go back to it. Windows removes it by itself after 10 days.

windowsCleanup.name: Temporary Setup Files
windowsCleanup.explanation: Files Windows Setup used during an upgrade and left behind. Safe to clean.

windowsCleanup.name: Discarded Upgrade Files
windowsCleanup.explanation: Files an upgrade set aside and no longer needs. Safe to clean.

windowsCleanup.name: Upgrade Log Files
windowsCleanup.explanation: Logs from Windows upgrades, used to look into one that failed. Safe to clean unless you're troubleshooting an upgrade.

windowsCleanup.name: Setup Log Files
windowsCleanup.explanation: Logs Windows Setup writes. Safe to clean.

windowsCleanup.name: Reset Log Files
windowsCleanup.explanation: Logs from resetting this PC. Safe to clean.

windowsCleanup.name: System Memory Dump
windowsCleanup.explanation: The memory snapshot Windows saved when it last crashed, often several gigabytes. Safe to clean unless you were about to send it to support.

windowsCleanup.name: System Minidumps
windowsCleanup.explanation: Small crash reports Windows saves each time it stops with an error. Safe to clean unless you're troubleshooting crashes.

windowsCleanup.name: Old Driver Versions
windowsCleanup.explanation: Earlier versions of drivers Windows keeps after an update. Afterwards you can't roll a driver back to one of them.

deviceBackups.explanation: A full backup of {device}, last made {date}. Remove it only if you have a newer backup, in iCloud for example, or no longer need that device's data.

node-modules.name: Node.js Packages
node-modules.explanation: Code libraries installed for this project. Safe to remove for a project you are not working on; npm install brings them back.

next-build.name: Next.js Build Output
next-build.explanation: Compiled pages and assets produced by Next.js. Safe to delete and rebuilt the next time you run or build the site.

nuxt-build.name: Nuxt Build Cache
nuxt-build.explanation: Temporary build files created by Nuxt. Safe to delete and rebuilt the next time you run or build the site.

nuxt-output.name: Nuxt Output
nuxt-output.explanation: The built site Nuxt produces for deployment. Safe to delete and rebuilt on your next build.

sveltekit-build.name: SvelteKit Build Cache
sveltekit-build.explanation: Generated files SvelteKit keeps between builds. Safe to delete and rebuilt the next time you run the project.

astro-build.name: Astro Build Cache
astro-build.explanation: Temporary build files created by Astro. Safe to delete and rebuilt on your next build.

angular-cache.name: Angular Build Cache
angular-cache.explanation: Build cache kept by the Angular CLI to make repeat builds faster. Safe to delete and rebuilt automatically.

turbo-cache.name: Turborepo Build Cache
turbo-cache.explanation: Saved build outputs from Turborepo. Safe to delete. Your next build simply takes a little longer.

parcel-cache.name: Parcel Build Cache
parcel-cache.explanation: Saved build outputs from the Parcel bundler. Safe to delete and rebuilt next time you run a Parcel build.

rust-target.name: Rust Build Output
rust-target.explanation: Compiled Rust project files. Safe to delete; your project recompiles on the next build.

venv.name: Python Environment
venv.explanation: A self-contained Python environment holding packages installed for this project. Safe to delete and recreated by reinstalling from requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.

pytest-cache.name: pytest Cache
pytest-cache.explanation: Test results and lookup data cached by pytest. Safe to delete and recreated the next time you run your tests.

mypy-cache.name: Mypy Type Check Cache
mypy-cache.explanation: Saved results from Mypy. Safe to delete and rebuilt next time Mypy runs.

ruff-cache.name: Ruff Linter Cache
ruff-cache.explanation: Saved results from Ruff. Safe to delete and recreated on the next run.

tox-environments.name: tox Environments
tox-environments.explanation: Throwaway Python environments tox builds to run tests in. Safe to delete and rebuilt on your next tox run.

dart-tool.name: Dart Tool Folder
dart-tool.explanation: A temporary folder used by the Dart and Flutter tools. Safe to delete and recreated the next time you run a Flutter command.

flutter-cache.name: Flutter Build Output
flutter-cache.explanation: Build files created by Flutter. Safe to delete and recreated the next time you build your app.

gradle-cache.name: Gradle Project Cache
gradle-cache.explanation: Build files and caches Gradle keeps for this project. Safe to delete; your next build recreates them.

maven-target.name: Maven Build Output
maven-target.explanation: Compiled classes and packaged output produced by Maven. Safe to delete and rebuilt by your next build.

gradle-build.name: Gradle Build Output
gradle-build.explanation: Compiled output produced by a Gradle build. Safe to delete and rebuilt by your next build.

sbt-target.name: sbt Build Output
sbt-target.explanation: Compiled output produced by sbt for a Scala project. Safe to delete and rebuilt by your next build.

dotnet-bin.name: .NET Build Output
dotnet-bin.explanation: Compiled programs and libraries produced by a .NET build. Safe to delete and rebuilt by your next dotnet build.

dotnet-obj.name: .NET Intermediate Files
dotnet-obj.explanation: Temporary files .NET creates while compiling. Safe to delete and recreated on your next build.

elixir-build.name: Elixir Build Output
elixir-build.explanation: Compiled output created by Mix. Safe to delete and rebuilt from your source the next time you compile.

elixir-deps.name: Elixir Dependencies
elixir-deps.explanation: Dependency source code downloaded by Mix. Safe to delete and re-downloaded on your next build.

composer-vendor.name: PHP Packages
composer-vendor.explanation: Third-party PHP packages downloaded by Composer. Safe to delete and re-downloaded by composer install.

bundler-vendor.name: Ruby Gems
bundler-vendor.explanation: Ruby gems installed into the project by Bundler. Safe to delete and reinstalled by bundle install.

stack-work.name: Stack Build Output
stack-work.explanation: Compiled output and dependencies kept by Stack for a Haskell project. Safe to delete and rebuilt by your next build, which can take a while.

cabal-dist.name: Cabal Build Output
cabal-dist.explanation: Compiled output produced by Cabal for a Haskell project. Safe to delete and rebuilt by your next build.

zig-cache.name: Zig Build Cache
zig-cache.explanation: Compilation cache kept by Zig. Safe to delete and rebuilt on your next build.

zig-out.name: Zig Build Output
zig-out.explanation: Programs and libraries produced by a Zig build. Safe to delete and rebuilt on your next build.

dune-build.name: Dune Build Output
dune-build.explanation: Compiled output produced by Dune for an OCaml project. Safe to delete and rebuilt by your next build.

cmake-build.name: CMake Build Output
cmake-build.explanation: Compiled output and build configuration produced by CMake. Safe to delete, though you need to configure and build the project again.

terraform-plugins.name: Terraform Plugins
terraform-plugins.explanation: Provider plugins and modules Terraform downloads for a workspace. Re-downloaded by terraform init.

godot-cache.name: Godot Project Cache
godot-cache.explanation: Imported assets and editor data Godot keeps for a project. Safe to delete and rebuilt the next time you open the project.

unity-library.name: Unity Library Folder
unity-library.explanation: Unity's imported-asset database for this project. It rebuilds itself, but reimporting a large project can take a long time.

unity-temp.name: Unity Temp Folder
unity-temp.explanation: Scratch files Unity writes while the editor is running. Do not remove it while the project is open in Unity.

unreal-intermediate.name: Unreal Intermediate Files
unreal-intermediate.explanation: Generated build files Unreal creates while compiling a project. They come back on the next build, which takes longer than usual.

unreal-derived-data.name: Unreal Derived Data Cache
unreal-derived-data.explanation: Cooked assets and compiled shaders Unreal caches for a project. Rebuilt automatically, but the first build afterwards can be very slow.
